title: Degree bound under constant subtraction
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space whose components indexed by sets of size greater than $k$ vanish identically. For every real constant $c$, the function $x\mapsto f(x)-c$ also has all components indexed by sets of size greater than $k$ vanishing identically.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $k\in\mathbb N$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of degree at most $k$, and $c\in\mathbb R$. Then $x\mapsto f(x)-c$ has degree at most $k$.
